A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ILGen work, with matching authors, method, and core experiments. The text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval experiments across seven benchmarks, comparisons with real and Objaverse training data, and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains original retrieval experiments and adds human verification, mixed-data training, instance-diversity studies, and rendered-viewpoint experiments.

M1.justification: The default generation pipeline, encoder training, and recall@k objective remain unchanged. v2 adds experimental procedural variants involving near-duplicate removal, feature-enriched generation prompts, and TRELLIS-rendered viewpoints before background generation (Appendices B and E). These extend the method without replacing its core procedure.

E1.justification: The same seven retrieval benchmarks and artwork, landmark, product, and generic domains remain. Appendix B adds a human identity-matching task involving four researchers and generated instances. The other new experiments vary training configurations within existing domain coverage.

E2.justification: Existing pretrained, Objaverse-background, real-only, and alternative-loss comparisons are retained. v2 adds comparisons against mixed real/synthetic training and a TRELLIS-based viewpoint-generation variant (Tables 5 and S5). These are additional training alternatives, rather than new standalone retrieval systems.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include a 40-question, four-choice human study with four researchers, real/synthetic mixing budgets, category-count versus instances-per-category sweeps, and sampling four of seven rendered viewpoints. Table 2 also revises the reported MET database from 397K to 224.4K; the PDFs do not establish whether this corrects documentation or reflects an actual evaluation change.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's existing model, loss, background, and Objaverse analyses, v2 adds identity verification, near-duplicate removal, prompt-diversity tests, generation-hyperparameter sensitivity, mixed-data training, rendered-viewpoint tests, and identity-preservation failure cases. Figure 8 supplements the existing visual overlap inspection with SSCD copy detection.

E5.justification: v1 reports point scores without training-seed counts or dispersion. v2 Table 3 specifies three seeds per trained setting and reports means and standard deviations across the main comparison. This substantially changes uncertainty reporting, although it does not establish a particular increase over v1's undisclosed run count; other comparisons largely remain point estimates.

E6.justification: Table 3 updates reported scores: ILGen-ALL's average changes from 52.6 to 52.7 ± 0.3, and Objaverse-background from 51.4 to 50.9 ± 0.5. New results include 96.25% human-verification accuracy, a 55.3 average with 20K synthetic plus 12K real instances, and 51.8 with rendered viewpoints. These are revised summaries and additional experimental results, not demonstrated same-setting gains between versions.

T1.justification: The retrieval formulation, descriptor definition, dataset-size expressions, and recall@k formulation are preserved. v2 empirically investigates the existing instance-identity assumption but introduces no new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The introduction extends the contribution from an alternative to real training data to both an alternative and a complement. The central claims about domain-driven synthetic instance generation and improved retrieval representations remain unchanged in the abstract and conclusion.

C2.justification: New interpretations address sensitivity to instance diversity, complementarity with real data, and possible reconstruction artifacts behind poorer rendered-view results. Appendix B explains identity failures and why changing landmark surroundings can be problematic. Appendix A adds substantive limitations concerning provenance, inherited cultural and geographical biases, and privacy-related misuse.

D1.justification: v2 adds code/pretrained-model access information and stated licensing restrictions, expands alpha-matting and padding implementation details, and documents new feature prompts, SSCD configuration, and TRELLIS rendering angles. These materially expand reproducibility information. Previously supplied loss hyperparameters and training-time information are mainly relocated into the main text.

R1.justification: v2 acknowledges Kalantidis et al. (2024) on generative augmentation for localization, replacing v1's characterization of Sundaram et al. as the only relevant prior generative approach. Additional citations support segmentation, SSCD, copy-detection thresholds, and TRELLIS. The broader related-work structure and positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most existing prose are preserved. Local revisions organize background generation into three explicit steps, move training/loss details from the appendix into Sections 4.1 and 4.3, and reorganize appendix headings around the added studies. There are also copyedits, affiliation-format changes, and acknowledgments.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 5 and supplementary Tables S1, S4, and S5, alongside extensive identity, diversity, study-interface, failure-case, copy-detection, and rendered-viewpoint visualizations. Existing supplementary figures are retained as S9 and S11 rather than removed. Table 3 is reformatted for mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting, and Table 4 gains experiment IDs.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for the central synthetic-instance premise through human verification, diversity tests, and failure analysis, while adding an SSCD overlap audit and three-seed uncertainty reporting. Implementation/access information and explicit limitations further improve assessability. The human study is small, mixed-data experiments use larger training sets, and Section 4.2 incorrectly claims an advantage over Objaverse especially on SOP despite Table 3 showing 55.6 versus 57.6. These shortcomings temper, but do not outweigh, the substantial evidential gains.
